question: A family used to buy 30 litres of mustard oil a month. Its price rises by 10% and then by another 50%, and the family lets its spending on mustard oil rise by 10%. How many litres does it buy now?
solution: Quantity = spending ÷ price, so it becomes 30 × 1.1 ÷ (1.1 × 1.5) = 30 × 1.1 ÷ 1.65 = 20 litres.

question: The price of lentils rises by 50%, so for ₹1,800 a family now gets 10 kg less than before. What is the original price per kg?
solution: At the new price, what ₹1,800 used to buy would cost 50% more, that is ₹900 more; ₹900 is the price of the 10 kg the family now goes without. New price = 900 ÷ 10 = ₹90 per kg. The original price = 90 ÷ 1.5 = ₹60 per kg.

solutionHi: नए मूल्य पर, ₹1,800 वाली पुरानी मात्रा 50% अधिक, यानी ₹900 अधिक में आती; ₹900 उन 10 kg का मूल्य है जो अब नहीं मिलते। नया मूल्य = 900 ÷ 10 = ₹90 प्रति kg। पहले का मूल्य = 90 ÷ 1.5 = ₹60 प्रति kg।

question: A taxi driver drives 20% slower than usual and reaches 25 minutes late. How many minutes does the trip take at the usual speed?
